reader_question: How often has the Senate voted on ending debate, Congress by Congress?
grade_line: Documented: the Senate’s own count of cloture votes
title: The Senate held 298 votes to end debate in 2019 and 2020, after no more than seven in any Congress before 1971.
reading_guide: Each circle is one two-year Congress, and its area is the number of votes on ending debate. One sentence sums the Congresses before 1971. From 1971 the circles sit at each Congress’s first year, alternately above and below the line so neighbors stay apart; on a phone each Congress takes its own row.
measure_line: Senate votes on cloture, a motion to end debate, on bills and nominations together, by Congress, from the 65th Congress (1917 and 1918), the first under the Senate’s cloture rule, to the 119th Congress through November 10, 2026, United States Senate.
notes: From 1917 to 1975, ending debate took two-thirds of the senators present and voting, except from 1949 to 1959, when it took two-thirds of the whole Senate. Since 1975 it takes three-fifths of all senators for most matters, and changes in 2013 and 2017 lowered it to a simple majority for nominations.
The counts mix bills and nominations.
The 119th Congress, 2025 and 2026, is still in session; a dashed outline marks its 295 votes through November 10, 2026.
alt: Bubble timeline of Senate votes on ending debate in each Congress from 1917 to 2026. A sentence sums the 27 Congresses before 1971, which held 49 votes in all and no more than seven in any one. From 1971 the circles grow through the 1970s to the 2000s and swell after 2007; the largest is 298 votes in the Congress of 2019 and 2020, and the current Congress has held 295 through November 10, 2026.

chart_notes: Circle area is in proportion to votes on cloture; the key shows 10, 100 and 300 votes. The 116th Congress, 2019 and 2020, which the title names, is drawn solid in the text’s ink; the others are gray with a thin outline. A dashed outline marks the 119th Congress, still in session.
